title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
central_claims: Stromal caveolin-1 drives p190RhoGAP/Rho-dependent matrix contraction, alignment and stiffening, increasing tumor invasion and metastatic potency.

source_manifest.title: Replication Study: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
source_manifest.finding: Fibroblast matrix contraction was supported; metastatic burden did not show the predicted pattern, with 45-day versus roughly70-day follow-up and imaging differences limiting interpretation.

source_manifest.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts lead tumor invasion through integrin-β3-dependent fibronectin assembly.
source_manifest.finding: Independent CAF experiments found fibronectin assembly necessary for invasion even with retained matrix contractility; this refines the mechanical-remodeling account.

source_manifest.title: Loss of Caveolin-1 in Metastasis-Associated Macrophages Drives Lung Metastatic Growth through Increased Angiogenesis.
source_manifest.finding: Independent work extends stromal Cav1 research to metastasis-associated macrophages, finding an anti-metastatic Cav1 function in that distinct compartment.

answers.rationale: Matrix remodeling is supported, but the focal Cav1-dependent metastatic advantage remains unresolved in the direct replication.
Shortened follow-up and imaging differences make the failed metastatic comparison inconclusive for the original full result.
The replication’s independent design cannot compensate for the substantially shorter metastasis observation window.
The sources retain parts of stromal remodeling while identifying cell-specific and temporal qualifications; no unambiguous authoritative retention of the complete causal chain was established.
Macrophage Cav1 has an opposite effect in a distinct compartment; this does not directly falsify or validate the original fibroblast-specific mechanism.
Celus and colleagues extend the stromal Cav1 question to bone-marrow-derived macrophages and establish a compartment-specific anti-metastatic mechanism.

research.summary: A mixed, technically qualified replication: Cav1-dependent contraction survives, whereas the metastatic prediction remains unresolved. Different Cav1 functions in macrophages are an extension, not proof that the fibroblast result failed.
